ops.title: A PATH-shimming test fixture can never be t.Parallel — the restriction is intrinsic, not an oversight
ops.body:
Go's testing package panics outright — `testing: test using t.Setenv, t.Chdir,
or cryptotest.SetGlobalRandom can not use t.Parallel` (`testing.go:1766`,
`checkParallel`) — on `t.Parallel()` in any test that has already called
`t.Setenv` or `t.Chdir`. Reproduced directly (Go 1.26.5, 2026-08-02), not
inferred from docs.

`internal/vcstest.Repo` makes ten `t.Setenv` calls (`fixture.go:245-265`) and one
`t.Chdir` (`fixture.go:237`), so **no test that builds a real-repo fixture can be
parallel**. This is not a defect to fix:

- The recording shim works by putting itself at the head of `PATH`, and `PATH` is
  process-global. There is no version of `Repo` that installs a shim without
  mutating process state.
- `t.Chdir` is separately load-bearing: the production code under test resolves
  its repository from the working directory.

Consequence for planning: the usual "add `t.Parallel()`, fixtures are TempDir-
isolated, ~8-way speedup" mitigation is UNAVAILABLE for this harness, and any
plan that budgets on it is wrong. Measured cost of converting off PATH shell
fakes onto real fixtures, without -race: `internal/vcs` 23.6s → 44.0s,
`internal/overview` 3.4s → 8.0s. Roughly 2x, at 61 fixture constructions per run
(~170ms plain git, ~380ms jj-colocated).

What IS available:
1. `t.Parallel()` on tests that build no fixture — pure parsers, measured-stream
   tables, argv tables. In cc-context that was 14 tests.
2. **One fixture per table rather than per case**, wherever the cases do not
   mutate the repo. Only genuinely-mutating cases need their own.
3. If more is needed, the lever is sharing across whole test functions, not
   within a table.

Related: [ambient git config reaching code under test] — the same `t.Setenv`
process-wide mutation that forbids `t.Parallel` is exactly what makes the
isolation correct.
